passage: You asked why I'm so strict about honesty, so listen. I'm Minakshi, and at twenty-four I was unfaithful to my partner Bhavna. I told myself Bhavna had been distant, that it was only once, that no one would ever know. Mostly I felt sick, afraid that someone would discover it, and under that, ashamed. One night Bhavna asked, "Is something wrong?" and the easy lie was right there in my mouth. I put the cup down and said, "Yes. I did something that hurt you, and I'm going to tell you." I didn't say it was Bhavna's fault. I didn't ask to be comforted. Bhavna cried and went to a sister's house for a week, and I had no right to ask for anything. Hiding would have been so much easier, and so much worse.

qa.q: How old was Minakshi when the unfaithfulness happened?
What was Minakshi feeling underneath the excuses?
qa.a: Fear of discovery, and under that, shame. Minakshi felt sick, and the excuses were a way of holding those feelings off.

qa.q: What did Minakshi do that faced the harm, and what would have made it worse?
qa.a: Minakshi told Bhavna the truth without blaming Bhavna or asking for comfort. Continuing to hide, or excusing it as Bhavna's distance, would have made it worse.

qa.q: How might Bhavna have felt hearing Minakshi's confession?
qa.a: Hurt and overwhelmed, since Bhavna cried and went to a sister's house for a week. Being told honestly, rather than discovering it, may still have mattered.

grounding: Shows someone who was unfaithful, torn between shame, self-justification and fear of discovery, choosing to face what they did without blaming the partner or asking to be soothed.

passage:
Kishore, sit. You're asking me why your aunt and I nearly separated when you were small? You're old enough now. When I was twenty-five, two years married, I had an affair with a woman at my office. Three months. I'm Ujjwal, your uncle, and I'm not proud of any of it.

When it ended, I was torn in pieces. Shame, yes. But also excuses: she was busy with her mother, she didn't understand me. And fear, every day, that she'd find out.

One night I nearly said to her, "You pushed me to it." I heard how ugly it was before it left my mouth.

So I told her the truth, all of it, without blaming her. She cried and shouted and left for her sister's. I didn't ask her to comfort me, though I wanted to. I went to a counsellor alone. It took four years before she trusted me again. That was the price, and it was fair.

qa.q: How long did young Ujjwal's affair last?
What was young Ujjwal feeling after the affair ended?
qa.a: Young Ujjwal felt torn between shame, excuses and fear of being found out.

qa.q: What turning point in the story led to the honest path?
qa.a: Ujjwal stopped himself from blaming his wife and told her the whole truth, then went to a counsellor instead of asking her to soothe him.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal's wife have felt when he told her?
qa.a: She felt deeply hurt and angry, crying, shouting and leaving for her sister's, and it took her years to trust again.

grounding: The elder's story shows a young husband torn between shame, self-justification and fear after being unfaithful, choosing to face the harm without blaming or seeking comfort.

passage:
Vinita had an hour before Ravi's train got in from Nagpur, and she had rehearsed three versions of the conversation. In the first, she said nothing and deleted everything. In the second, she told him, but explained that he was always away, that she had been lonely, that it just happened. In the third, she told him the truth and didn't defend it.

The affair with a man from her yoga class had ended two weeks ago. The shame hadn't. Neither had the fear.

She called Aditi, her oldest friend. "If I tell him, can I at least explain why?"

"You can say you were lonely. Don't make it his fault. And don't ask him to make you feel better tonight. That's not his job."

The train was twenty minutes late. Vinita sat in the car outside the station, hands cold. When Ravi got in, she said, "I need to tell you something I did. It was wrong, and it's mine."

qa.q: Where was Ravi's train coming from?
qa.a: Ravi's train was coming from Nagpur.

qa.q: What was Vinita feeling in the hour before the train arrived?
qa.a: Vinita felt torn between shame and fear, rehearsing ways to hide, justify or confess.

qa.q: What did Aditi advise, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Aditi said not to blame Ravi or ask him to comfort her, because the honest path means owning the harm without shifting it.

qa.q: How might Ravi feel hearing Vinita's opening words?
qa.a: Ravi is likely to feel shocked and frightened, sensing something serious is coming.

grounding: The story shows a young wife torn between shame, self-justification and fear after infidelity, choosing honesty without blaming her partner or seeking comfort.
